calibration.question: Select the evidence bundle with an approved cohort denominator.
calibration.compact_view: A contains authorized Q1/Q3 cohort rows; B contains a current company-wide percentage.
calibration.full_view: A contains the cohort ledger and its denominator rule; B has no cohort-level denominator.

candidates.label: approved cohort ledger
candidates.compact_evidence: The calibration ledger is scoped to approved sample records for Q1 and Q3. The question asks for a cohort rate, not a company-wide service level. Its row schema contains committed and on_time counts.
candidates.full_evidence: Calibration ledger rows identify quarter, approved_sample_cohort scope, status, committed_orders, and on_time_orders. The effective 2026 rule includes approved sample rows and excludes cancelled, pending, legacy, and out-of-period records. The weighted rate is sum(on_time_orders) divided by sum(committed_orders); row percentages must not be averaged. Source locators resolve to the calibration ledger and active rule.

candidates.label: company-wide review
candidates.compact_evidence: The calibration review reports company-wide quarterly on-time delivery. It has no approved sample cohort denominator and cannot support the requested cohort calculation.
candidates.full_evidence: The operating review gives one aggregate on-time delivery percentage for each company quarter. It does not expose approved-sample committed or on-time counts, does not identify the sample cohort, and does not define the cohort's effective scope rule. These aggregate percentages are context only and are not a valid denominator for the requested weighted sample rate.

cases.question: For approved sample records in 2026Q1 and 2026Q3, calculate weighted on-time delivery as sum(on_time_orders) / sum(committed_orders). Choose the evidence bundle that supports this cohort calculation; do not use a company-wide rate.
cases.compact_view: A is the approved sample ledger with committed/on_time rows; B is an overall company review percentage.
cases.full_view: The sample ledger contains Q1/Q3 cohort rows and the active denominator rule. The overall review has no cohort denominator.

candidates.label: approved cohort ledger
candidates.compact_evidence: Source register entry for Nova regional delivery, frozen 2026-09-18 by the network performance data office. The bundle covers Q1 and Q3 sample records and carries stable record ids, region, quarter, order counts, status, scope, and rule-id fields. Its catalogue describes an approved regional cohort and identifies a sample ledger, but does not put the effective status test or rule dates in the compact index. The period includes the same two quarters named in the question. The extract is distinct from the operating review and preserves individual rows rather than one headline percentage. It has a source revision, a custodian, and row locators suitable for checking what was included. The index alone does not resolve whether every row belongs in the requested denominator. The register lists twelve regional entries per quarter and preserves separate pending, cancelled, and legacy examples; it does not publish a computed rate. The underlying row order and document locator are retained for source review.

candidates.label: company overall review
candidates.compact_evidence: Source register entry for Nova's 2026 operating review, issued for the first three quarters after the warehouse slotting rollout. It contains an authoritative metric table with quarterly company on-time-delivery percentages and narrative about carrier coverage, route density, weekend service, and approved management actions. The compact index calls it a company operating review and does not list regional order-count columns. It spans Q1 and Q3 and is an authorized source for company-level delivery context. The review's metric table is stable and its prose explains changes in carrier performance, so it could be relevant to a delivery question. The index does not identify a sample-cohort view, but that distinction must be checked against the full report before treating it as a denominator source. The report also records management actions and operational causes, but those narrative sections do not alter its document class. Its quarter table gives one percentage per company quarter and no record identifiers. The compact entry is an index description, not a conclusion about sample eligibility.

cases.question: Compare approved sample Orion expedited fees and exception counts for 2026Q1 and 2026Q3, apply the effective approval scope, and report the fee delta. Choose the evidence bundle that supports the sample calculation, not a company-wide metric.
cases.compact_view: A is a current sample ledger; B is the company operating review. Both are authorized and discuss expedited freight in overlapping 2026 periods.
cases.full_view: The ledger carries the row-level sample scope and active approval rule; the operating review provides company-level cost context without the same sample rows.

candidates.label: current sample ledger
candidates.compact_evidence: Source register entry for Orion expedited freight and exception costs, frozen 2026-09-18 by manufacturing finance control. The bundle covers Q1 and Q3 and includes stable transaction ids, region, quarter, fee and exception fields, status, scope, and rule-id values. It is described as a current sample extract and shares the same cost vocabulary and reporting period as the other authorized candidate. The compact index lists neither the active rule dates nor the row-by-row treatment for pending, cancelled, or legacy entries. It preserves source locators and a revision boundary, and the document remains separate from the company operating review. Its title and topic make it a plausible cost source, but the index does not state which rows qualify for the approved sample total or whether a prefiltered quarterly delta is present. The register covers more than one region and preserves transactions in posting order. It has no precomputed Q1/Q3 answer field; the analyst must reconcile the source rows with the scope control. The index does not expose that reconciliation.

candidates.label: company operating review
candidates.compact_evidence: Source register entry for Orion's 2026 operating review, issued after consolidation of the Cedar Park assembly lines. It covers the first three quarters and discusses expedited freight, supplier qualification, recurring cost pressure, and operational exceptions. Its metric table is authoritative for company-level measures, while its narrative provides context about late-August freight and Q3 margin pressure. The compact catalogue uses the same business terms as the sample-cost question and identifies a period that overlaps Q1 and Q3. It does not list a row-level approved-sample ledger in the index. The report is authorized and could explain why freight cost moved, but the compact view alone does not show the unit of scope behind any relevant aggregate cost or whether the reported material supports an exception-count total. It also describes delivery and supplier actions elsewhere in the report, which may provide context for cost changes. The source register exposes the report id and quarter coverage but no approved-sample record count. The title is similar enough to the current extract that the scope needs inspection.

cases.question: For approved Nova sample records in Q1 and Q3, calculate weighted on-time delivery using sum(on_time_orders) / sum(committed_orders). Choose the source that exposes the eligible cohort and denominator; do not substitute an overall percentage.
cases.compact_view: A is a report overall rate; B is a cohort ledger with committed and on_time counts.
cases.full_view: Only the cohort ledger contains the valid denominator and effective scope needed for weighted delivery.

candidates.label: overall rate
candidates.compact_evidence: Source register entry for Nova's company review, with quarterly delivery measures and narrative about carrier coverage changes. The review covers the same Q1 and Q3 period requested and its metric table is the authority for company performance. Its index identifies aggregate on-time-delivery rates but does not list a per-region order table, approval status, or sample rule. The prose discusses weekend coverage, route density, and the effect of carrier misses, which are relevant to interpreting a delivery trend. The source is authorized for operating context and has a stable document id. The compact entry does not decide whether those company-level measures can be reused for a sample cohort; the full evidence has to be checked for the numerator and denominator required by the question. Its catalogue groups all service areas under the company name and identifies narrative sections as contextual sources. The index contains no approved-sample row count or committed/on-time record pairs. It describes a useful performance trend, but leaves the requested cohort interpretation to the full source review.

candidates.label: cohort delivery ledger
candidates.compact_evidence: Source register entry for a frozen Nova regional delivery extract, with one record id per regional posting and fields for quarter, region, committed orders, on-time orders, status, scope, and rule id. The catalogue calls the records a controlled sample cohort, but it does not expose the active 2026 rule text or say which status and scope values survive filtering. Both requested quarters are represented, and the extract is maintained separately from the company review. Its row-level structure appears suitable for a weighted calculation, although the compact index does not establish whether all displayed records belong in that denominator or whether the row percentages can be averaged. Stable locators permit a later full-text check. The index lists twelve regional postings for each quarter and identifies a small number of records in other workflow states. It contains no computed rates and preserves the extract revision for verification. Those catalogue details describe file shape and provenance, not a validated answer.

cases.question: Determine whether the Orion Q3 exception can be included in approved-sample expedited fees. Inclusion requires a final approval signature; conflicting unsigned records must produce insufficient_evidence.
cases.compact_view: A and B are authorized records for the same exception, but the final approval signature is missing.
cases.full_view: The expanded view confirms the records conflict and no final sign-off exists; the correct result is insufficient evidence.

candidates.label: include
candidates.compact_evidence: Source register entry for the finance analyst's Orion Q3 inclusion proposal. It links exception ORI-Q3-EX-044 to a Cedar Park priority-carrier invoice and an approved-sample program. The record describes a shipment, fee, purchase-order association, and a preliminary controller review. Its index identifies a proposed include treatment and an archive revision, but does not show a final disposition value or signed-by identity. The evidence package has invoice, receipt, purchase-order, and workflow references. It is authorized for the frozen Q3 cost-control corpus and appears directly related to expedited sample fees. The compact view does not establish whether a preliminary review completes the approval requirement or whether another signed record supersedes this proposal. The index also reports the document custodian and field families but not a terminal workflow state. It is a source description intended to distinguish the analyst submission from the audit entry, not a statement that the proposed treatment is valid.

candidates.label: exclude
candidates.compact_evidence: Source register entry for the Orion controller audit desk's Q3 hold on exception ORI-Q3-EX-044. It links the same carrier charge, purchase order, receipt, and sample program as the finance submission. The index describes an exclude-pending-review treatment and identifies an audit date and archive revision. It is authorized for the same frozen cost-control corpus. Its compact catalogue lists a proposed hold, not a terminal status, and does not expose a final signed decision or later amendment reference. The entry is relevant to the question because it challenges the proposed inclusion, but its index does not establish whether the audit hold is a completed rejection or a temporary control state. The register distinguishes the audit desk's role from the submitting analyst and keeps the original proposal as a separate source. Its locator points to the audit-side entry and does not replace the finance record. The index gives custody and revision information without asserting a final eligibility result.
